title: Payment connection pool timeouts
executive_summary: payment-service's DB connection pool (payment-db-pool) was cut from max_size 50 to 10 by a config change at 10:04Z (cfg-56d39584, author config-bot, ticket OPS-2669). Pool utilisation rose to 100% and requests began timing out acquiring connections from 10:06Z, producing a ~17% error rate and ~12% timeout rate. Postgres connection use fell at the same time, consistent with fewer pooled connections rather than database distress. This is a self-inflicted configuration regression, not a connection leak like last year's incident.

hypotheses.description: Config change reducing db.pool.max_size from 50 to 10 at 10:04Z exhausted the payment-db-pool, causing connection acquisition timeouts. Mechanism: Pool capacity dropped 80%. Under steady ~300 rps, demand exceeds 10 connections, so waiters queue (waiting=15-92) and hit the 5000ms acquisition timeout, yielding errors and timeouts. Onset of pool saturation (10:05-10:06) follows the config change (10:04) and precedes the error onset (10:06).

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): configuration_regression in payment-service - Config change reducing db.pool.max_size from 50 to 10 at 10:04Z exhausted the payment-db-pool, causing connection acquisition timeouts.
corrective_actions: Revert db.pool.max_size from 10 to 50 on payment-service (OPS-2669) and confirm pods reload the value.
Confirm pool waiters drain and error/timeout rates return to baseline (~0.8% / ~0.1%).
preventive_actions: Add validation in CI/config pipeline rejecting pool sizes that drop more than a set fraction without approval.
Require review for config-bot changes to database pool settings.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on payment-db-pool utilisation above 80% and on any pool-acquisition timeout log.
Track db.pool.max_size as a config-drift metric.
limitations: Live pod configuration was not verified against the config-change record.
Latency symptom is not reflected in p99 metrics; per-request failure latency was not examined.
auth-service and redis metrics were not queried.

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The incident is most likely a configuration regression: db.pool.max_size was cut from 50 to 10 at 10:04Z, which saturated the payment DB pool and caused acquisition timeouts from 10:06Z. The timing, the pool-exhaustion log signature, and the healthy Postgres side all support this. It is not confirmed because I did not verify the live pod config, and the flat p99 latency does not match the reported latency symptom. Last year's leak pattern is only an analogy and is not supported by the data.
